page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 8 GB of RAM, yielding a 2.0 GB per core memory ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server allocates 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled (2 threads per core). The processor is equipped with a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It includes advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512). No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with Geekbench single-core and text processing scores placing in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also show strong results in the top 25%. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations exhibit limitations. The Passmark memory score falls into the bottom 10%, and memory bandwidth tests for both read and write operations are categorized in the bottom 25%. Multi-core CPU performance under stress-ng and Passmark CPU tests also register in the bottom 25%, reflecting the physical core limit of two cores.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highcpu-4 offers a highly dense compute profile for workloads that prioritize single-threaded execution speed and specialized vector or matrix instructions over massive memory capacity. It is well-suited for lightweight web serving, text processing, and software compilation. It is less optimal for memory-intensive databases, large-scale multi-threaded processing, or heavy LLM text generation, where its limited 8 GB memory capacity and lower memory bandwidth present clear performance tradeoffs.
